historicalContracts.name: Euro Coin Token
historicalContracts.note: Circle's L1 EURC FiatTokenProxy tracked only via L1USDCGateway reference; EURC is not counted in scroll TVS and the EURC gateway is deliberately not critical, so its upgrades (Circle ops) put no scroll funds at risk.

historicalContracts.name: L2WETHGatewayCounterpart
historicalContracts.note: Phantom entry: the L1WETHGateway address resolved on the scroll chain (unverified immutable contract, no values or permissions); nothing on either chain trusts the scroll-chain address, so its compromise reaches no funds; removed by the cross-chain discovery refactor.

historicalContracts.name: L1MessageQueue
historicalContracts.note: Core ProxyAdmin-upgradeable queue gating all L1->L2 messages and popped by ScrollChain at batch finalization: a compromised queue injects deposit messages that credit unbacked ETH on L2 (stealing from the messenger escrow) or bricks finalization, freezing withdrawals; its successor L1MessageQueueV2 is critical today.

historicalContracts.name: L1BatchBridgeGateway
historicalContracts.note: Deposit-side batching helper that forwards ETH L1->L2 like any user; never a TVS escrow in scroll config and holds no permission over the canonical escrows, so compromise only touches in-transit deposits not counted as project funds.

historicalContracts.name: L1ScrollMessengerCounterpart
historicalContracts.note: Phantom entry: the L1ScrollMessenger address resolved on the scroll chain via L2ScrollMessenger.counterpart (unverified immutable contract, no values or permissions); no L1 contract trusts this address as an L2 message sender, so compromise reaches no funds.

historicalContracts.name: L1ETHGatewayCounterpart
historicalContracts.note: Phantom entry: the L1ETHGateway address resolved on the scroll chain via L2ETHGateway.counterpart (unverified immutable contract, no values or permissions); L1 gateways only honor their real L2 counterpart addresses, so compromise reaches no funds.

historicalContracts.name: L1StandardERC20GatewayCounterpart
historicalContracts.note: Phantom entry: the L1StandardERC20Gateway address resolved on the scroll chain via an L2GatewayRouter reference (unverified immutable contract, no values or permissions); the L1 escrow only honors its real L2 counterpart, so compromise reaches no funds.
